verdict.rationale: Skyvern publishes its source in a public GitHub repository (Skyvern-AI/skyvern), and its llms.txt calls it an open-source platform. A community member independently identifies the license as AGPL-3.0, an OSI-approved open license; their remark that AGPL rules it out for their employer is a licensing preference, not a contradiction. Self-hosting docs (pip, Docker Compose, Kubernetes) show the server code is usable on your own infrastructure. Missing for 10: a first-party license statement in the docs, and clarity on whether cloud-only features (e.g. the Copilot and Studio builders) are also in the open repository.
